title: Comparative Cosmography Population Wave 002 — Garden, Boundary Water, Judgment, Intermediate States & Divine Mountain
purpose: Populate underdeveloped House functions: protected garden, sacred/source waters, guarded return, postmortem punishment, oath-boundary river, intermediate-state transition, divine mountain-city and royal/protective serpent symbolism.
epistemic_rule: Own-tradition meaning and dated reception come before Potatoverse placement. Similar functions do not imply a universal hidden system.

entries.source_summary: Genesis 2–3 presents Eden as a planted, watered garden containing the Tree of Life and Tree of Knowledge. A river waters the garden and divides into four branches. After expulsion, cherubim and a flaming sword guard the way to the Tree of Life. Later Jewish and Christian traditions develop Eden/Paradise in multiple earthly and heavenly directions.
entries.structural_use: High-value Garden-regime comparator: cultivation, nourishment, knowledge/choice, river-source, boundary, exclusion and guarded return all meet in one complex.

entries.source_summary: The Eden narrative describes one river watering the garden and then dividing into four named branches, producing a source-to-world distribution motif.
entries.structural_use: Strong water/source/return comparator: Garden does not merely contain life; it distributes outward.

entries.source_summary: After expulsion from Eden, cherubim and a flaming sword guard the way to the Tree of Life.
entries.structural_use: Guarded-threshold comparator: access to Life may be directional, conditional and protected rather than permanently open.

entries.source_summary: Gehenna derives from the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, associated in biblical texts with condemned child-sacrifice practices; later Jewish and Christian traditions use Gehinnom/Gehenna for postmortem punishment in diverse ways.
entries.structural_use: Excellent provenance-to-reception example: a historical place acquires eschatological/judgment meanings. Keep it distinct from Sheol and Hades.

entries.source_summary: Styx is both an underworld river and goddess/personification. Classical sources make its water the binding oath of the gods and place it within Hades-related geography.
entries.structural_use: Boundary-water + oath comparator: a river can be legal/relational infrastructure as well as terrain.

entries.source_summary: Bardo translates an intermediate/transitional state; in Tibetan Buddhism it commonly refers to the state between death and rebirth and can also name broader sets of transitional states across life, death and rebirth.
entries.structural_use: Strong route/state comparator for transition without forcing a fixed Heaven/Below geography.

entries.source_summary: Olympus is the mountain-home and palace/acropolis complex of the Olympian gods in Greek epic reception, with gates, divine halls and Zeus's seat.
entries.structural_use: Useful Mountain + House/City + divine-council complex. It demonstrates that a sacred mountain can also function as inhabited architecture/regime.

entries.source_summary: Zeus is ruler of the Olympian gods in Greek tradition, closely associated with sky, thunder, kingship, oath/order and the Olympian divine council.
entries.structural_use: Divine-order/kingship comparator connected to Olympus and Styx oath traditions.

entries.source_summary: The uraeus is the rearing cobra worn on the royal brow; Metropolitan Museum material describes it as a symbol of royalty associated with the goddess Wadjet and protective power.
entries.structural_use: Serpent + crown/royal office + protection comparator, useful precisely because serpent symbolism here is protective/sovereign rather than simply adversarial.

resulting_rules: Garden/Paradise should be modeled as a protected generative regime with source-water, Trees, boundary and guarded access—not simply as Heaven.
Underworld and punishment must be separated: Sheol/Hades/Hel/Duat are not automatically Gehenna/Hell.
Intermediate-state traditions such as bardo may be routes/states rather than places on a fixed floor.
Sacred water can act as boundary, oath, nourishment, purification, memory or death-crossing depending tradition.
Serpent imagery must be function-led: protective royalty, healing, wisdom, chaos, adversary, renewal and other meanings remain distinct.
A sacred mountain may also be an inhabited House/city/regime; category can be primary with secondary functions rather than forcing one label.
